acceptanceCriteria: DONE: computes and itemises the category final value fee, the per-order fixed fee, the seller-standing surcharge, the insertion fee past the free allotment, promoted listings, the international fee and the dispute fee, from sale price, shipping, tax, category, store tier, listing format and standing. The AC asked for one. eBay prints no effective date on either fee page, so an effectiveFrom would be a date we invented, and a made-up freshness stamp is worse than none. src/lib/ebay-fee-schedule.ts carries EBAY_FEES_RETRIEVED_ON instead and the page states it, which is checkable.

DONE: 17 tests in src/lib/__tests__/ebay-fee-schedule.test.ts, every expected number hand-computed in a comment beside it. Includes the free-insertion crossing on an Anchor auction, the handbag cliff where a $2,001 sale costs LESS than a $1,999 one, and the athletic-shoe threshold where the rate drops and the per-order fee stops.

THE SCHEDULE IS THREE SHAPES, not one rate, which is what every naive fee calculator gets wrong. Apparel is MARGINAL (13.6% up to $7,500, then 2.35%). Handbags are a CLIFF (crossing $2,000 re-rates the whole sale). Athletic shoes are CONDITIONAL (at $150 the rate drops AND the per-order fee stops). Starter Store gets no discount at all.

SIDE EFFECT, and the most valuable thing in this story: src/lib/ebay-fees.ts carried 13.25% for apparel. That is a real eBay rate belonging to Coins & Paper Money and the trading cards, not apparel. It is read by ScoutAI buy/skip and by the composer profit estimate, both of which have been understating fees by 0.35 points in the seller favour. Corrected in both copies of the mirror, and in the reader-facing fee figures on 16 comparison pages and the where-to-sell guide.

userStories.title: eBay shipping calculator at /tools/ebay-shipping-calculator
userStories.description: As a seller pricing a listing, I want to compare shipping cost by weight, dimensions and service, so that I do not lose margin by guessing postage.
acceptanceCriteria: Takes weight, package dimensions, origin and destination ZIP, and returns a compared table of the services a clothing seller actually uses, including a flat-rate versus weight-based recommendation. Rate data is a dated static table with an `effectiveFrom` field, not a live carrier API call, so the page prerenders and cannot break on a third-party outage. DONE. USPS_RATES_EFFECTIVE_FROM is 2026-08-08 and is printed on the page. Zone comes from a packed table of 896 ZIP-prefix centroids built from the Census 2020 ZCTA gazetteer, so even the zone lookup makes no network call.

Dimensional weight is applied and shown as its own line when it exceeds actual weight, since that is the case sellers get wrong. DONE, with the three 2026-07-12 rule changes modelled: divisor 139 (was 166), dimensions rounded up to the whole inch before anything is measured, and the one-cubic-foot floor below which dimensions are ignored entirely.

Targets `ebay shipping calculator` (50,000/mo, Low) as primary and `cheapest way to ship clothes` (500/mo) as secondary, both registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE, plus two more secondaries and four question targets.

A unit test covers a dimensional-weight case and a flat-rate-cheaper case. DONE, 16 tests in src/lib/__tests__/usps-rate-schedule.test.ts, including the puffer-jacket dim case (2 lb on the scale, billed at 19 lb) and both directions of the flat-rate comparison.

SOURCING, which is the part that took the time: every number was read off a published rate sheet and confirmed against a second independent source before it was allowed into the code. Source A is Pirate Ship's August 8 2026 USPS rate workbook, source B is USPS Notice 123 at pe.usps.com. They agree to the cent on all 20 values checked. The working is in docs/seo/usps-rate-schedule-CONFIRMED.csv, following the rule US-9003 produced after its first draft had 13.25% for apparel.

PRICE TIER IS STATED, not implied. These are USPS commercial prices, the tier an online label buys. eBay's own rates are at or below it, so the page says a result is a ceiling rather than a quote, and says counter prices run 30-40% higher.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: Ground Advantage charges ONE price per zone under a pound and it is LOWER than the 1 lb price ($6.93 vs $7.61 in Zone 1). A package crossing 16 oz costs more. That cliff got its own table on the page and its own test, because it is the cheapest thing a clothing seller can act on.

userStories.title: Reseller profit calculator that takes CONDITION as an input
userStories.description: As a reseller deciding whether an item is worth listing, I want a profit calculator that factors the item's condition into the estimated sale price, so that I get a realistic number rather than one based on a mint-condition comp.
acceptanceCriteria: Inputs cost of goods, marketplace, sale price, shipping, and a condition grade on the 1.0-10.0 scale; outputs gross, fees, net profit, margin and ROI. DONE. The marketplace selector reuses the US-9005 fee schedules, so all five platforms are priced by the same code the fee calculators use.

The condition input adjusts the estimated sale price using the same tier definitions the grading engine uses, and the page states the adjustment applied rather than hiding it. DONE, and the tier function is now SHARED rather than duplicated: tierLabelForGrade moved out of whats-it-worth.tsx into src/lib/condition-value-curve.ts and both surfaces import it.

TWO grades, not one. The calculator asks what condition the COMP was in as well as the item, because a comp taken from a mint listing overstates a worn item and a comp from a beaten one understates a clean one. Every competing calculator assumes the comp is mint and can only adjust downward, which is why sellers using them under-price good stock.

A 'grade this item' call to action links to the grading flow, and the link carries a PostHog property so the calculator-to-grading path is measurable. DONE. New registry event calculator_grading_cta_click with the {source, destination} property shape already used by comparison_crosslist_cta_click, so US-9010 can read both funnels off one shape.
Targets `reseller profit calculator`, `ebay profit calculator` and `resale profit margin calculator`, registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE.

A unit test asserts that two identical items differing only in condition grade produce different estimated sale prices, and that a 10.0 grade applies no downward adjustment. DONE, 12 tests in src/lib/__tests__/condition-value-curve.test.ts.

THE MULTIPLIERS ARE MEASURED, NOT INVENTED, which was the real work in this story. They are derived from GradeThread's own public Condition Index: 53 published curves resting on 3,811 eBay sold comps, each grade's median divided by that curve's grade-10 median, then the median of those 53 ratios. scripts/seo/derive-condition-value-curve.mjs re-runs it against live data and reproduces the committed table exactly.

WHAT THE NUMBERS ARE NOT is stated in the module and on the page: each Index curve is anchored on three measured bands of up to 25 comps, and the grades between anchors are the Index's own interpolation. So it summarises 159 measured bands, not 3,811 independent observations of ten grades.

THE SPREAD IS PUBLISHED NEXT TO THE AVERAGE. At grade 9.0 the ratio runs 0.527 to 1.000 across the 53 items, so the page prints the range beside every median and tells the reader to look at it first. When the seller picks a specific Condition Index item, the calculator uses that item's own measured curve and says which of the two it used.
FOLLOW-UP: US-2280 (regress realized FlipDesk outcomes against assigned grades) would replace this derived curve with an outcome-grounded one. The module names it.

userStories.title: Fix the two underperforming comparison pages: poshmark-vs-mercari and depop-vs-poshmark
userStories.description: As a seller choosing where to list, I want a comparison that covers how each marketplace handles condition disputes and returns, so that I can pick on the terms that actually cost me money. CORRECTED 2026-08-18: this story originally asked to CREATE these two pages, on the claim that the comparison family held only mercari-vs-ebay. That claim came from grepping the COMPARISONS array in comparison-guides.ts, which holds one entry; the other 15 comparison routes are registered in public-routes.ts. Both pages have been live since 2026-07-06 with ~1,400 words each. The work is to fix them, not build them.
acceptanceCriteria: DIAGNOSED 2026-08-18, and the premise is wrong for the third time in this file. The pages are not the variable: which platforms they name is. All 16 comparison pages ship from one template on one publish date, and they split cleanly -- every pair naming Grailed or Vinted ranks in the top 15, every pair made only of eBay, Poshmark, Mercari and Depop ranks at 20 to 45. Full table and the two ruled-out confounds in docs/seo/compare-family-diagnosis.md.

Two alternatives ruled out rather than assumed. More words did not help: /compare/mercari-vs-ebay is the hand-written flagship and ranks 39th on 2 impressions, worse than 13 template pages. More internal links did not help: the only two pages carrying named anchor sets in interlink-rules.ts were poshmark-vs-mercari (44.8) and mercari-vs-ebay (39), so the confound runs backwards from the fix-the-page hypothesis.

DONE: the interlink anchor budget moved to /compare/vinted-vs-mercari (position 8.5) and /compare/grailed-vs-poshmark (position 11.0). Internal authority is worth spending where a page can cross a threshold into the top five, not on a page at 44.8.

DONE under US-9017: titles and meta descriptions rewritten for the four comparison pages that earn impressions. The other twelve keep the template, because there is nothing to learn from rewriting a page nobody sees.

RESOLVED 2026-08-18, operator said yes. /compare/depop-vs-poshmark now canonicalises to /blog/depop-vs-poshmark-which-should-you-use. The page stays live and stays linked from the hub; only the canonical and the sitemap entry changed. PublicRoute gained an optional canonicalPath, head-builder and the SPA both honour it, and functions/_shared/sitemap.ts skips any route carrying one, because advertising a URL you have just told Google to ignore is a contradictory signal. 6 tests in src/test/canonical-overrides.test.ts lock the target, the carry-through, and the absence of canonical chains.
Do NOT expand the competitor-alternative family: all three pages (Vendoo, List Perfectly, Crosslist) already exist, vendoo alternative is 500/mo and list perfectly alternative returned blank.

Do NOT build more head-term comparison pages. The family covers all 16 pairs, and the ceiling on the incumbent pairs is set by competition a ten-week-old site cannot outspend. The pages that rank are the pairs nobody else bothered to write.

VERIFIED IN CODE, not taken on trust from the note: the interlink anchor sets are on /compare/vinted-vs-mercari and /compare/grailed-vs-poshmark in interlink-rules.ts; the US-9017 rewrite for vinted-vs-mercari is in the worklist marked shipped; and the returns/condition-dispute row the story's description asks for already exists for all seven platforms in comparison-guides.ts, feeding a wedge row on every one of the 16 pages.
userStories.notes: Rewritten 2026-08-18 from Search Console evidence. Original premise (family holds only mercari-vs-ebay) was false: 16 live /compare/ URLs, 15 registered via public-routes.ts rather than the COMPARISONS array. Diagnosed 2026-08-18. The repair this story asked for would not have worked: rewriting poshmark-vs-mercari harder is the thing already tried on mercari-vs-ebay, which is the worst-ranking page in the family. Everything actionable is done; one operator decision is open.

userStories.title: FlipDesk conversion landing pages for the high-bid commercial terms
userStories.description: As a seller who has just finished a fee calculation, I want a page that explains the tool that would do this automatically, so that I have somewhere to go other than back to the search results.
acceptanceCriteria: SUPERSEDED: one page per job-to-be-done for the five commercial terms. The diagnosis in AC2 said not to build them and the revised scope in AC7 replaced this. No new head-term landing page was built.

DIAGNOSED 2026-08-18 before writing anything. /reselling/best-crosslisting-apps IS the page this story proposed to build and it ranks 51.5 on 203 impressions, while every other crosslisting URL on the site ranks in the top 11. Full table in docs/seo/crosslisting-cluster-diagnosis.md.
These are judged on CONVERSION RATE, not search position. DONE: the funnel is instrumented and documented.

Each page has a single primary call to action into FlipDesk signup, and states the condition-grading differentiator that separates it from Vendoo and List Perfectly. DONE. /flipdesk/crosslisting gained a section that NAMES both competitors, concedes they cover more marketplaces, and argues the one axis where FlipDesk differs: they move your description between sites, they do not produce evidence about condition.

A PostHog funnel is defined from calculator view to landing page view to signup start, and registered in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. DONE. commercial_landing_view fires on MOUNT rather than on a click, because a conversion rate needs its denominator; commercial_landing_signup_start on the primary CTA; crosslist_listicle_vendor_handoff on the listicle handoff, using the same {source, destination} pair as US-9018 and US-9006.
Registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE for /flipdesk/crosslisting. It was already in the marketing sitemap segment via flipdeskLandingRoutes().

REVISED SCOPE ACTED ON: no second head-term landing page. Commercial intent now has a route to /flipdesk/crosslisting from the listicle, on a section that says plainly the listicle is not the place we argue for our own product.

THE LISTICLE STOPPED PRESENTING ITSELF AS NEUTRAL, which is the half of the trust problem a rewrite can actually fix. It called itself an 'honest roundup' with no disclosure that GradeThread builds one of the five tools it ranks. It now carries that disclosure above the fold, marks its own row in the at-a-glance table, and tells the reader to check the other four on their own sites.
The $34.51 top-of-page bid was treated as a warning, not a target, per AC8. Nothing was built for it.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING: US-9005's four fee calculators share one parameterised component, but ROUTE_PAGE_MODULES derives 'tools/{slug}', so four routes pointed at files that do not exist and their chunk preload silently did nothing (the US-1950 regression). The existing lockstep guard compares the KEYS of two maps built from one source, so it can only catch a typo. Calculator gained an optional pageModule, and src/test/route-page-modules-exist.test.ts now resolves every module id against the filesystem.
userStories.notes: Evidence added 2026-08-18 from the Search Console export. See docs/seo/unserved-query-clusters.md. Diagnosed 2026-08-18. The build this story asks for would have landed on page five next to the page that is already there.

userStories.title: Wire the calculators into the FlipDesk funnel and measure the handoff
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know how many calculator visitors become signups, so that I can tell whether Path 3 is an acquisition channel or just traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: Every calculator page carries a contextual call to action into the matching FlipDesk surface, placed after the user has a result rather than before. DONE for all eight, rendered immediately above the FAQ block. MATCHED, not generic: fee calculators to /flipdesk/bookkeeping, the four marketplace ones to /flipdesk/crosslisting, the profit calculator to /flipdesk/comps, the measurement converter to /flipdesk/inventory-management. A test asserts at least three distinct surfaces, because if everything pointed at one page the per-calculator conversion rate would have nothing to distinguish.

PostHog events fire for calculator_used, calculator_cta_clicked and signup_started_from_tool, each carrying the calculator slug; all three are registered in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. DONE, plus a FOURTH the story did not list and AC3 requires: calculator_view. Without the arrival count there is no denominator, and 'acquisition channel or just traffic' is a rate.

calculator_used is deliberately NOT a view. It fires once, on the first input change, so a visitor who read the Store-tier table and left can be told apart from one who typed their own numbers in. Those convert very differently and conflating them makes the rate meaningless.

ATTRIBUTION SURVIVES THE HOP, which is the part that would have quietly broken. The handoff goes to the matching /flipdesk/* page, not to /signup, so the calculator slug rides across in a `from` query parameter (TOOL_SOURCE_PARAM), the landing page reads it back, and signup_started_from_tool fires only when it is present. Without it every tool-driven signup would be credited to the landing page.

A dashboard or saved query reports calculator sessions, call-to-action click rate and signup conversion per calculator slug. DONE as far as it can be from here: all four query DEFINITIONS are written in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. The dashboard itself is built in PostHog by hand and is operator work. Note the handoff rate is defined over USED rather than over VIEW, because the question is whether someone who got a result wants the product.

OPEN, DATED, NOT GUESSED: a baseline is recorded 30 days after the first calculator ships. The first shipped 2026-08-18 (US-9003), so the baseline is due 2026-09-17. It must not be invented before the window closes, because US-9016's kill criteria compare against it and a fabricated baseline makes them unfalsifiable. The date and the four rates to record are in the vault note.

7 tests in src/lib/seo/__tests__/calculator-funnel.test.ts: every live calculator has a handoff, every handoff points at a FlipDesk landing that exists, the surfaces are not all the same, the copy is not placeholder copy, and all four events are declared.

userStories.title: [GATE] SERP-check five repair terms before committing to the damage-and-care build
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know who actually holds the top ten for the repair keywords, so that we do not commit to a 295,750/mo cluster that is locked up by domain-authority-80 incumbents.
acceptanceCriteria: Record the top ten organic results for the five terms. DONE, 2026-08-18, all five, 39 results recorded in docs/seo/repair-serp-check.md. Stated plainly in that note: this is a search-API sample, not a rank-tracker snapshot, so it answers WHO occupies the space and does not establish any URL's exact position.

For each, note how many of the ten are major publishers versus reachable sites, and whether any result is thin enough to displace. DONE. Across all 39 results there is EXACTLY ONE major publisher (Fox News, on an AMP real-estate URL). None of Tide, Persil, Good Housekeeping, Real Simple or Martha Stewart appears anywhere. The space is held by small craft blogs, clothing and appliance brand blogs, and UGC.

SIX OF 39 SLOTS ARE VISIBLY WEAK: a jewellery company ranking first for a sweater-snag query, Speed Queen's Thailand page for a US search, two spam PDFs on a hijacked New Zealand government domain, one more on a hijacked university domain, and a London waste-authority leaflet.
GATE RESULT: Path 1 is NOT blocked. AC3's kill condition is not met and it is not close. Path 1 is not recorded as blocked in the strategy note; the verdict and evidence are written into it instead.

Write the verdict and the evidence into the Path 1 section of the strategy note. DONE, in vault/40-growth/seo-strategy-options-2026-08.md, replacing the 'kill condition has not been tested yet' paragraph and reinforcing 'The risk Path 1 carries' with the same evidence.

THE FINDING THE STORY DID NOT ASK FOR, and it changes what Path 1 is worth rather than whether it is possible: not one of the 39 results is a resale, grading or secondhand-clothing site. The two closest are Oxfam, a charity shop, and Levi's. So there is no incumbent to displace, AND Google does not read these queries as resale-shaped and the visitor behind them is not a seller. The whole risk moves onto topical dilution.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DOWNSTREAM STORIES, which is what a gate is for: US-9015 (containment) is reprioritised ahead of US-9013 and US-9014, because the boundary is cheap now and expensive after a hundred care pages exist. US-9013's entry terms are challenged in that story's own notes.

userStories.title: Reframe the flaw library from disclosure-first to removal-first under /care/
userStories.description: As someone who just found a stain on a garment, I want a page that tells me how to get it out, so that I land on GradeThread for the question I actually asked rather than one about listing terminology.
acceptanceCriteria: The entries each gain a removal-and-prevention section that comes BEFORE the existing disclosure-and-grading section, and titles are rewritten from grading language to removal language. DONE for all of them. NOTE THE COUNT: the story says 35 and there are 32. The removal block sits directly under the definition, above 'How to spot it'; grade impact, fixability and disclosure now sit below it, because those are our questions and not the reader's.

EVERY ENTRY DECLARES WHETHER IT COMES OUT, and 11 of the 32 say no. That is the differentiator and it is enforced by a test: a laundry blog has to promise a fix to justify the page, and we do not, so a 'no' entry says so in a banner in the first line rather than selling the reader an afternoon of scrubbing. 5 are yes, 16 are sometimes, 11 are no.

Pages are served under a /care/ path prefix, separate from the reseller spine, per the containment decision in the strategy note. DONE. FLAW_LIBRARY_HUB_PATH moved from /grading/flaws to /care, and because every consumer went through that constant and flawPath(), the router, prerender, head-builder, JSON-LD and sitemap all followed.

Existing flaw-library URLs 301 to their /care/ equivalents, and the redirect map is covered by a test so a rename cannot silently orphan them. DONE, two rules in public/_redirects, and 9 tests in src/test/care-redirects.test.ts.

THE REDIRECTS WERE WRITTEN BELOW THE /* CATCH-ALL FIRST, which would have 404'd all 32 old URLs while looking correct in the diff. public/_redirects is first-match-wins. A test now asserts the ordering, not just the presence, because presence is the easy half.

Each page ends on the honest hinge that some damage does not come out, linking down into pricing and grading. DONE, and the copy changes with the verdict: a permanent flaw gets 'It is staying, so the question is what it costs'. The three links out go to /resale-value-by-condition, /condition-grading and /tools/reseller-profit-calculator. One way only; US-9015 guards that nothing points back up.

keyword-targets.ts entries are updated from disclosure keywords to removal keywords; keyword-targets.test.ts passes. DONE, four entries under a NEW `care` cluster. The cluster is separate on purpose: the containment decision only means something if this content can be measured apart from the reseller spine, and US-9016's kill criteria read it as its own line.

THE FOUR TARGETS ARE THE ONES US-9011 CLEARED, not the highest-volume ones: unshrink clothes, snag in a sweater, broken zipper, hole in jeans. `how to sew on a button` is 50,000/mo and deliberately absent, because the gate found it is the purest non-adjacent intent in the set.
`npm run ui:check` still reports zero for src/. DONE, 0 blocking.

COLLATERAL, RECONCILED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: /grading/flaws/elastic-degradation had its SERP copy rewritten under US-9017 earlier the same day. The worklist CSV now records the /care URL and the title that is actually live, marked yes-superseded-by-us-9012, and docs/seo/ctr-rewrite-pass.md explains it. The 301 carries the CTR baseline across; the 2026-10-17 follow-up should read the new URL.

The public-routes router guard needed a /care clause. The 32 concrete paths are served by one dynamic /care/:flaw route; under /grading/ they were covered by the glossary clause, so the move made the guard report all 32 as missing from the router.

userStories.title: Repair entry pages for the two 50,000/mo Low-competition terms
userStories.description: As someone with a broken zipper or a missing button, I want a step-by-step repair guide, so that I can fix the garment myself.
acceptanceCriteria: SUPERSEDED BY THE GATE: full guides for both 50,000/mo terms. The zipper guide shipped. The button guide did NOT, per AC7, and a test asserts its absence so it cannot be added back without someone deciding to.
Build the repair sub-cluster before stain removal. DONE. Seven repair guides, no stain-removal guides.

Each guide carries HowTo JSON-LD with real numbered steps, tools and materials, emitted from head-builder.ts as well as the SPA route. DONE, and verified in the built HTML: /care/snags-pulls ships one HowTo, six HowToStep and two HowToTool nodes with totalTime PT10M and a per-step fragment URL.

THE MARKUP AND THE PAGE ARE ONE ARRAY. The HowTo is built from the same steps the page renders, so it can never describe steps a reader cannot see. Google's own HowTo documentation names that as the first failure, and it is the easy mistake to make when structured data is written separately from copy.

Remaining repair terms are covered by the same template. DONE: hole in jeans, snag in a sweater, darn a hole in a sweater, broken belt loop, stretched-out collar, and the zipper. Six of the seven named terms; `how to replace a zipper pull` is covered inside the zipper guide rather than as its own entry.
Registered in keyword-targets.ts and in the /care/ sitemap segment. DONE, seven entries in the care cluster, and the segment is functions/sitemap-care.xml.ts from US-9015.

ONE URL PER INTENT, which is the design decision worth recording. The guides attach to the EXISTING /care entries rather than creating a second /care/repair/* family. A reader searching `how to fix a snag in a sweater` and one searching `what is a snag` want the same page; splitting them would leave two thin URLs competing for one query.

ENTRY TERMS FOLLOWED THE GATE, not the volume. The two 5,000/mo terms it cleared (snag in a sweater, unshrink clothes) both got guides, and both are condition defects with a resale consequence, which is the only bridge from repair intent back to the product.

DEFECT CAUGHT BY A GUARD, worth recording because the guard nearly did not exist: extending howToLd() for tools and times wrote `url: undefined` onto every step of pages with no step URLs, which serialises into the node. jsonld-schema-lint.test.ts failed 38 routes including /how-it-works and every garment guide. Fixed with a conditional spread; the comment says why.
userStories.notes: Entry terms challenged by the US-9011 gate on 2026-08-18. Evidence in docs/seo/repair-serp-check.md. The zipper term is still worth doing; the button term is the one to drop.

userStories.title: Flaw-crossed-with-fabric matrix, only where the answer genuinely differs
userStories.description: As someone with a specific stain on a specific fabric, I want advice for that combination, so that I do not ruin a silk blouse using a method written for denim.
acceptanceCriteria: A generated page family crossing the flaw taxonomy with the fabrics that behave differently, seeded from the existing fabric taxonomy rather than a new list. DONE. Six fibre classes MIRRORED from FiberClass in services/edge-functions/src/lib/fabric-criteria.ts, the grading engine's own taxonomy, with a test that reads that file and fails if the two drift.

A combination only gets a page when the procedure genuinely differs; combinations whose answer is identical to the parent are NOT generated. DONE: 18 pages out of a possible 192. Every entry carries a `differs` line stating what changes; if you cannot write that line, the combination does not get a page.

A test asserts no generated page duplicates its parent's procedure. DONE, two of them: an exact-match check on every step against the parent's removal steps, and a looser check that no entry is mostly the parent's text with words moved.

NO THIN CANONICALISING PAGES. The AC allowed generating the other 174 and canonicalising them to the parent. They are simply not generated instead, because a page that exists only to point at another page is still a page Google crawls and judges. A test asserts that /care/pilling/linen and friends have no route at all.

This is the test a programmatic family has to pass and the reason this one is allowed where Path 4's value pages were not. Holds: getting a stain out of silk forbids the enzyme detergent that is step one on cotton, because silk is a protein and so is the stain.
Page count is logged at build time so silent growth is visible. DONE, in vite.config.ts: `[seo] care cluster: 51 pages, of which 18 are flaw-by-fabric (cap 400); 20.9% of 244 static routes`.

If the matrix exceeds 400 pages, the story stops and the cap is re-argued rather than shipped. MATRIX_PAGE_CAP is declared with that instruction next to it. Worth noting the cap was never the binding constraint: we are at 18 of 400. The binding constraint is having something different to say.

Every generated page is registered through a calculatorRoutes()-style spread into PUBLIC_ROUTES and appears in the /care/ sitemap segment. DONE via careMatrixRoutes(), and because the pages live under /care they inherit every US-9015 containment guard automatically.

MARKUP: Article, not HowTo, even though the pages have numbered steps. The parent flaw page already claims the HowTo for the task where one exists, and two HowTo nodes competing over one procedure is exactly the over-marking Google's guidance warns about.

CAUGHT MY OWN GUARD BEING WRONG: US-9015's containment test asserted the care cluster was exactly 33 pages. That is a tripwire that fires on intended growth while saying nothing about unintended growth. It now computes 1 + flaws + matrix, and the 40% ceiling assertion is the one guarding the actual risk.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 THIS SHIPPED 18 ORPHANED PAGES AND CLOSED. Measured against production, not inferred: every one of the 11 parent flaw pages linked ZERO of its fabric children. /care/rust-spots served 30283 bytes and not one href="/care/rust-spots/silk", and the same held for all eleven. The pages were in the sitemap, registered in PUBLIC_ROUTES, prerendered and reachable by URL, with nothing pointing down at them.  THE TELL WAS FILED UNDER THE WRONG HEADING THE WHOLE TIME. matrixEntriesForFlaw is documented "Every fibre page that exists for a flaw, for the parent page to link down to" and had no callers, so audit-file-local-exports reported it as a DEAD EXPORT - one of eight to delete. It was not dead code. It was a missing section, and the audit cannot tell those apart because both look like an export nobody imports.  AND THE POLICY WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. interlink-rules.ts states it: "a pillar links all its cluster children in a curated chapter block (enforced by the pillar page components)". Nothing enforced it. care-matrix.test.ts asserted every entry is REGISTERED in PUBLIC_ROUTES, which is a different question and reads as coverage.  FIXED: FlawPage renders a "What changes by fabric" section from matrixEntriesForFlaw. Each row carries the child's own `differs` line rather than just its title - the same one-line test the matrix uses to decide a combination deserves a page at all, so the block is worth reading rather than a list of links wearing a heading. It renders nothing for the seven flaws with no child yet.  GUARDED: two cases in care-matrix.test.ts under "the matrix is wired and bounded", beside the registration case whose limits they expose. Sabotage- verified 3 of 3 with a green control either side - the section removed (the original state), the link target hard-coded instead of per-entry, and the entries derived twice.  Also corrected while in there: flaw-library.tsx's header still described these as /grading/flaws pages. US-9012 moved them to /care and routes/index.tsx says so; the header did not.

userStories.title: Containment guards so the care cluster cannot dilute the reseller entity
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the care content structurally separated from the reseller surface, so that Google's read of what GradeThread is does not drift toward laundry advice.
acceptanceCriteria: A test asserts no /care/ URL appears in the primary navigation, the homepage, or the top tier of the sitemap. DONE, 12 tests in src/test/care-containment.test.ts. The care cluster now has its OWN sitemap segment, functions/sitemap-care.xml.ts, listed after the two commercial segments rather than folded into sitemap-marketing.xml.

NOTE ON THAT TEST: the homepage assertion first read src/pages/home.tsx, which does not exist. It would have passed by accident forever. The homepage is src/pages/landing.tsx. A containment guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard, because it is also a claim that the containment holds.

A test asserts the interlink rules allow /care/ pages to link INTO the reseller spine but not the reverse. DONE. /care is its own hub in interlink-rules.ts, checked FIRST in hubForPath (a care page talks about grading and would otherwise fall into the grading hub on a keyword). isCrossHubLinkAllowed refuses every link INTO care, including from the otherwise-unconstrained non-hub pages such as the homepage and the legal pages, and lets care pages link out freely.
HUB_PILLARS is typed Record<Exclude<Hub, "care">, string>, so giving care a pillar that cross-hub links could legally reach is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a quiet hole in the containment.
Care content stays on the main domain in a subdirectory, NOT a subdomain. DONE and asserted: a subdomain would split the authority this cluster exists to build, which is the only thing it is for.

The ratio of care URLs to reseller URLs is reported by the sitemap build; the rationale for the chosen ceiling is recorded in the vault. DONE. careRatio() in functions/_shared/sitemap.ts returns care URLs as a share of all static URLs, and a test asserts we are under the ceiling today (33 of ~226, about 15%).

THE CEILING IS 40% AND THE REASONING IS WRITTEN DOWN, because it is a decision rather than a measurement. The full Path 1 build roughly doubles today's 15%. 40% is the last point at which the commercial and grading segments together are still clearly the majority, and it leaves room for US-9014 to land without renegotiating the boundary. Recorded so the next person argues with the reasoning instead of the number.

Path 1 is documented in the vault note as an authority and link engine, not an acquisition channel. DONE, in its own section. 295,750/mo of volume, of which 1,550 carries seller intent: 0.5%. Judged as acquisition it will look like a failure at every review and somebody will correctly kill it for missing a target it was never built to hit.

userStories.title: Kill criteria and cluster tracking for the rebuilt SEO paths
userStories.description: As the operator, I want each new cluster measured against a threshold set in advance, so that the next review reads the numbers instead of rationalising them.
acceptanceCriteria: A Search Console cluster view per path, one row each, extending the existing views. DONE, three rows added to vault/40-growth/seo-distribution-and-measurement.md: ^/tools/ (Path 3), ^/care/ (Path 1) and ^/care/[^/]+/[^/]+$ (the fabric matrix on its own). Compare and flipdesk already had rows.

THE MATRIX GETS ITS OWN ROW ON PURPOSE. US-9014 shipped 18 pages out of a possible 192 on the argument that only genuinely-different combinations earn a URL. If that argument is wrong, those 18 will show it by earning nothing while the parent pages earn something, and that is only visible if they are counted separately.

Thresholds set BEFORE the data arrives. DONE, with real DUE DATES rather than 'month 4': tools >= 2,000 impressions/mo by 2026-12-18; care >= 10,000 impressions/mo by 2027-02-18; FlipDesk landings explicitly NOT judged on impressions, on signup_started_from_tool / commercial_landing_view instead.

EACH THRESHOLD NAMES THE DIAGNOSTIC TO RUN WHEN IT MISSES, which is the lesson from the criterion that fired. Under 2,000 at position 30+ is competition; under 2,000 at position 5-15 is demand and the bucketed estimate was wrong. Those need different responses and an impressions number alone cannot tell them apart.

The depth test is recorded as a RATIO, not a count. DONE: at least 55% of a path's submitted terms above 50/mo, with a floor of 12 terms submitted so the ratio cannot be gamed by submitting four and clearing three. Recomputed against the 2026-08 pull for all five paths; Path 3 goes from failing on a technicality to passing at 61%.

A quarterly re-pull of the keyword CSV is scheduled. DONE: 2026-11-18, 2027-02-18, 2027-05-18, with the instruction that a change in path ordering is a finding for the strategy note rather than a silent edit to the table.

The July 2026 grading-cluster kill criterion is marked as FIRED. DONE, quoted verbatim and kept rather than replaced, because a kill criterion that gets deleted when it fires is not a kill criterion. Recorded with what it got right (more pages were not the answer) and what it got wrong (it assumed no demand or no indexation, and US-9001 found the site ranked fine at 0.85% CTR against a 3-10% baseline).

GUARD ADDED, not just a note: src/test/cluster-views.test.ts, 9 tests. Every documented regex must match a registered route, the thresholds must carry real dates, and the depth rule must still be a ratio. The failure mode is specific and it happened this week: US-9012 moved the flaw library to /care, and a saved view built on the old regex keeps working, reads zero and looks exactly like the cluster collapsing.

The certificate regex is a NAMED exception with its reason, not a loosened assertion: certificate URLs are edge-SSR'd and enter the sitemap via the edge API, so they are legitimately absent from the static registry.

userStories.title: Answer the migration intent on the comparison pages that already rank for it
userStories.description: As a reseller who has decided to switch marketplaces, I want the page to tell me how to move my listings, not which platform is better. CORRECTED 2026-08-18 before building: this story originally asked for a new /migrate/{from}-to-{to} family. Checked first, and ALL 13 migration queries already have a live /compare/ page for that exact pair, ranking at position 10 to 30. Building a parallel family would split authority against pages that already rank, on a site whose measured problem is authority concentration and CTR rather than page count. The work is one template change reaching all 16 comparison pages, and zero new URLs.

FLOORS AND HINTS ARE SEPARATE TYPES, and conflating them is the error the whole module is built around. A printed copyright year and a tagless neck label are FLOORS: hard, and nothing overturns them. A CONFLICT SUPPRESSES THE RANGE rather than printing beside it. A number next to "these tells disagree" is the half people remember, so the result returns latest: null and says so in words.

userStories.title: The query shape decides the click, and only three of thirteen target SERPs still return links
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know which of our target queries Google still answers with links rather than with an AI Overview, so that the next quarter is not spent ranking for results pages that have no results.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE: thirteen target queries checked in a browser for AI Overview, People Also Ask and organic link count, recorded in docs/seo/serp-feature-audit-2026-08-28.md with the method and the caveats.

THE RESULT IS SHARPER THAN EXPECTED. Three of thirteen carry no AI Overview and all three are NAMED TOOL NOUNS: "ebay fee calculator", "poshmark fee calculator", "brand authenticity checker". Every question-shaped or topic-shaped query in the set carries one. "vguc meaning" returned no organic links at all in the captured region.

IT EXPLAINS THE SITE'S OWN SPLIT, which had been the open puzzle: ten /tools URLs out-click 122 blog posts at 3.46% against a 0.73% site average, while 87 /grading URLs sit at position 8.6 and convert at 0.33%. The tempting read was that tool pages are better pages. They are not. Tool queries still have clickable results pages and informational queries do not. Same site, same authors, same internal linking.
CONFIRMED AGAINST OUR OWN TWO BEST PAGES: /tools/authenticity-check earns 10.98% CTR and /tools/fit-checker 12.5%, and both of their head terms are on the clean list.

CONSEQUENCE 1, and it retires an argument rather than opening one: the glossary cluster is NOT recoverable by writing. Eighty-seven URLs at a good position converting at 0.33%, on a query whose SERP returns zero organic links. Depth cannot fix a results page with no results. Their remaining value is internal linking and AI citation, and US-9016 should measure them on that rather than on clicks.

CONSEQUENCE 2, stated because it is uncomfortable: FOUR OF THE FIVE PAGES BUILT ON 2026-08-28 target AI-Overview queries. That was not known when they were scoped. They are still worth having, because they are the best answers on their terms and an AI Overview cites sources, but their click forecast should be halved.

CONSEQUENCE 3: the fee calculators shipped 2026-08-18, TEN DAYS before the Search Console window closed. Their position 25-49 is an unevaluated page, not a failing one. Do not touch them, and do not read US-9016's December threshold before they have had a full quarter.

THE PROCESS CHANGE IS THE POINT: query shape is now a build criterion. A 50,000/mo question-shaped keyword with an AI Overview is worth less than a 500/mo tool noun without one, and nothing in the process could tell those apart until now. Check the head term before committing to a cluster.

It was true of nine of thirteen. | ONE SAMPLE PER QUERY, signed in, desktop, US. AI Overview presence varies by user and over time, so re-run alongside the quarterly keyword pull US-9016 already schedules for 2026-11-18. This is a snapshot that changes a decision, not a measurement that settles one.

userStories.title: Size the five unmeasured clusters: authentication pulled now, the other four in six weeks
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the gaps in our own keyword research measured before the next build, so that the next quarter is chosen from evidence rather than from what the last two pulls happened to ask for. 776 keywords across two pulls and five clusters have zero coverage between them.
acceptanceCriteria: AUTHENTICATION PULLED 2026-08-28 at the owner's direction; the other four wait until roughly 2026-10-09 so the pages shipped this week have a quarter of data. Evidence: docs/seo/authentication-cluster-2026-08-28.md and docs/seo/keyword-pull-2026-08-28-authentication.csv (945 rows).

NOT VIA KEYWORD PLANNER, and the reason is a boundary rather than a limitation. The integration exists (services/edge-functions/src/lib/keyword-research.ts) but running it needs production Ads credentials and spends against the owner's account. Used 109 Google autocomplete probes across 20 brands and 5 templates instead, deduplicated to 945 distinct queries.

THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: autocomplete returns no volume, so the avg_monthly column in the CSV is EMPTY and should stay empty rather than be guessed at. What it returns is the query space and the shape distribution. This repo's own record argues that is the more reliable half anyway: US-9001 found three of four "proven 5,000/mo" URLs earning zero impressions after ten weeks.

THE CLUSTER IS REAL AND UNIFORM: 945 queries, 20 brands at 37-49 queries each, five repeating shapes. real-vs-fake 253, how-to-spot 205, how-to-tell 172, TOOL NOUN 101, fake-{part} 43. That uniformity is exactly what makes a 20-page programmatic build look obvious.

THE OBVIOUS BUILD IS THE WRONG BUILD, and the check that killed it took about forty minutes. US-9026 found named tool nouns are the one shape without an AI Overview; the hypothesis was that "{brand} authenticity check" would inherit that. It does not. SIX OF SEVEN brand-specific tool nouns carry an AI Overview (north face, carhartt, lululemon, stone island, patagonia, legit check app; only moncler was clean). Attaching a brand loses the exemption, because brand-plus-question is precisely what an AI Overview answers well.

WHERE THE CLEAN SERPS ACTUALLY ARE: the two commercial service terms. "clothing authentication service" (no AI Overview, 9 organic) and "brand authenticity checker" (no AI Overview, 9 organic, and GradeThread already ranks there at position 12.7 on the page that converts at 10.98%). That is one page strengthened, not twenty built.

THE INCUMBENTS ARE REACHABLE, not publishers: LegitApp, LegitGrails, RealAuthentication and TrussArchive, plus each brand's own help page and Reddit. LegitApp runs the per-brand page play at legitapp.com/what-we-authenticate/{brand}, so the pattern is commercially proven and simply not currently clickable for most brands.

RECOMMENDATION, recorded so it is not re-litigated from the query count: do NOT build 20 brand pages; own the two commercial head terms where the SERP is clean; use the 945 brand queries as DEPTH inside /tools/authenticity-check rather than as URLs, feeding the checker's own brand knowledge; and recheck Moncler, since one clean sample is not a finding.

ROOT CAUSE FIXED, not just noted. DEFAULT_SEED_KEYWORDS carried seven seeds and not one was authentication-shaped, which is why two pulls sized this cluster at a single keyword. A keyword tool only finds neighbours of what it is given, so an absent seed is an invisible cluster with no error message. Seven seeds added covering all four remaining gaps, with 3 tests in services/edge-functions/src/tests/keyword-seeds_test.ts asserting each cluster has a root and that the original product seeds survive.

STILL OPEN: the other four clusters (reseller tax and bookkeeping, platform how-to, "what is my X worth", vintage dating beyond single stitch), to be pulled around 2026-10-09. The "what is my X worth" pull matters most of the four because it is retroactive: /value is 15 URLs and /condition-index is 29, they earned 2 clicks in 94 days, and neither cluster was ever sized. Forty-four pages rest on an untested hypothesis.

The last two builds were both improved by checking before writing (US-9021 lost a feature the platform cannot support, US-9019 lost 700 words it did not need), and the pattern is that the cheap check changes the plan. | AUTHENTICATION DONE 2026-08-28, the rest deferred six weeks on the owner's call. | THE REUSABLE LESSON IS THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS: discovery found 945 queries and a clean five-shape template, which argued for twenty pages. The SERP-shape check then found six of seven of those head terms are AI-Overview'd, which argues for one. Volume said build; shape said do not. Shape was cheaper to measure and decided it.

userStories.title: Stop reading the 94-day average as the current number
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the reporting window matched to a site that is still ramping, so that decisions are not made against an average that is two thirds noise. The site went from 0.3 impressions a day in late May to 555 a day in the last fortnight.
acceptanceCriteria: THE CORRECTION, and it is a factor of four: the 94-day window to 2026-08-26 averages 4,072 impressions and 32 clicks a month. The LAST 14 DAYS run at 555 impressions and 4.57 clicks a day, which is 16,654 impressions and 137 clicks a month. The first third of the window contributed 9 impressions in 31 days. Averaging across it describes a site that no longer exists.

Daily trend for the record, from Chart.csv: first third 0.3 impr/day and 0 clicks, middle third 46 impr/day and 0.19 clicks/day, last third 354 impr/day and 3.03 clicks/day, last 14 days 555 impr/day and 4.57 clicks/day.

THE ONE NUMBER THAT DOES NOT IMPROVE ON THE SHORTER WINDOW IS CTR: 0.82% over the last 14 days against 0.73% over 94. So the click-through problem is current and real, and it is not an artifact of averaging. Everything else was.

AVERAGE POSITION IS DRIFTING WORSE AS IMPRESSIONS GROW (10.6 to 24.9 over the eight days to 2026-08-26) AND THAT IS NOT A DECLINE. It is the signature of new pages entering the index at depth and adding impressions there. Reading it as a ranking loss would be the expensive mistake, and it is the one the raw chart invites.

Fix the cluster views in vault/40-growth/seo-distribution-and-measurement.md to report a trailing 28-day window alongside the 90-day one, and say which of the two each threshold in US-9016 is judged on.

Re-date the US-9016 thresholds that were set against the old baseline, or state explicitly that they were set on 90-day figures and are being read on 90-day figures. Either is fine; mixing them is not.

THE PRACTICAL RULE, written where the next reader will hit it: nothing shipped in the last 8 weeks can be judged yet, and that currently includes the fee calculators (2026-08-18), the care cluster (2026-07-06 onward) and everything built on 2026-08-28.
